entries.clue: Charge in detention (7)

blocks.note: charge as in care or guardianship: 'the children in her charge'
detention as in being held by the police

annotation.surface: A police report: someone has been charged while held in the cells.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'charge' a criminal accusation, but here it means care or keeping, as in 'the children in her charge'.
annotation.definitionFit: Custody is both guardianship of someone and imprisonment awaiting trial.

entries.clue: Upper-class nob somehow entered match, resistant to pressure (7)

indicatorNotes.somehow: the letters of NOB are arranged in some other way
indicatorNotes.entered: the pieces are entered one after another

blocks.note: U = upper-class, the old label for posh usage
NOB rearranged
to match a couple is to wed them

annotation.surface: A posh toff somehow gets into a match and stands firm under pressure.
annotation.walkthrough: A nob is British slang for a toff, which the surface uses as a person; here it is just three letters to jumble. U for upper-class is a standard crossword abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone unbowed has not bent or given in under pressure.

entries.clue: Stand for bone-shaped biscuit, perhaps (5)

blocks.note: the verb: to stand someone a drink is to pay for it
a dog's reward biscuit; 'perhaps' marks it as one example

annotation.surface: A display stand for dog biscuits in a pet shop.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stand' reads as a noun, a rack or holder; it is the verb meaning to pay for someone, as in 'I'll stand you lunch'. 'Perhaps' flags the biscuit as just one example of a treat.
annotation.definitionFit: To treat someone is to stand them something; a dog's bone-shaped biscuit is a treat.

entries.clue: Take up help with the French court in regional language (7)

indicatorNotes.Take up: in a down clue, taking a word up writes it bottom to top

blocks.note: aid = help, then taken up to DIA
le = 'the' in French
CT is the standard abbreviation for court

annotation.surface: Someone takes up an offer of help at a French court conducted in the local tongue.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Take up' sounds like accepting an offer; in a down clue it tells you to write the next word upwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A dialect is a form of a language particular to one region.

entries.clue: Loosen a limit around island for rebel force? (7)

indicatorNotes.Loosen: a loosened limit has its letters shaken free to rearrange
indicatorNotes.around: the rearranged letters go around the island's letter

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 6 letters, arranged as MILIT…A
I = island, as on maps; it sits inside MILIT…A

annotation.surface: Authorities relax a restriction around an island to make way for an insurgent army.
annotation.walkthrough: The anagram of A LIMIT goes around I, giving MILIT(I)A. The question mark admits a militia need not be rebels.
annotation.definitionFit: A militia is an irregular armed force, often one raised against the government.

entries.clue: Midwest state barring a restaurant from the East (6)

indicatorNotes.barring: barring means excluding, so the A is taken out

blocks.note: Indiana is a US state in the Midwest
remove the final A

annotation.surface: A Midwestern state bans an Asian restaurant.
annotation.walkthrough: In Britain 'an Indian' is everyday shorthand for an Indian restaurant or takeaway, which is why the answer can stand for 'restaurant'.
annotation.definitionFit: An Indian, in British usage, is a restaurant serving food from India, in the East.

entries.clue: Approaching where a hang-glider might like to be? (2,3,4)

annotation.definition2: where a hang-glider might like to be

blocks.note: approaching as in coming soon, likely to happen

blocks.clueFragment: where a hang-glider might like to be
blocks.note: taken literally: a glider needs moving air

annotation.surface: A hang-glider coming in to land, wondering where they would rather be.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second half is the idiom read literally.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom, from hunting: game could smell a hunter coming on the wind; the second half takes the phrase literally for a glider riding air currents.

entries.clue: First person, no good judge, is unappreciative type (7)

blocks.note: I is the first-person pronoun
NG = no good, a standard abbreviation
to rate is to judge or assess

annotation.surface: A person who is useless at judging turns out to be ungrateful.
annotation.walkthrough: 'First person' looks like the winner of a race; it is the grammatical first person, I.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: ingrate comes from Latin ingratus, unthankful, so it names the kind of person who shows no appreciation.

entries.clue: Exploit others’ work transforming ancient ghetto (3,2,2,3,3)

indicatorNotes.transforming: transforming changes the form of the words, rearranging their letters

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters

annotation.surface: Developers profit from others' labour by redeveloping an old ghetto.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests gentrification; the definition is the idiom for muscling in on something others started.
annotation.definitionFit: To get in on the act is to join in something successful started by others, to share the benefit.

entries.clue: Talented brother of Cain, we’re told (4)

indicatorNotes.we’re told: what we are told is heard, not read, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: Abel was Cain's brother in Genesis

annotation.surface: Scripture tells us Cain's brother was gifted.
annotation.walkthrough: Abel and able are pronounced the same, so the Bible name is spelt as the adjective.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe someone with the skill or gift to do something well.

entries.clue: A cadet gone off to get some brief accounts (10)

indicatorNotes.off: letters that are off have gone wrong, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

annotation.surface: A trainee officer has left to fetch some short reports.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gone' looks like part of the indicator 'gone off', but its letters are fodder: A CADET GONE is the ten letters, and 'off' alone does the mixing.
annotation.definitionFit: Anecdotage means anecdotes collectively, a body of short stories told about people.

entries.clue: Broad area in Cornish region with fluctuating heat (6)

indicatorNotes.fluctuating: fluctuating heat keeps changing, so its letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.with: with joins the two parts side by side

blocks.note: Cornwall lies in the South West of England, SW
HEAT rearranged

annotation.surface: A wide stretch of Cornwall experiences changeable temperatures.
annotation.walkthrough: Cornwall is the county at England's south-western tip, so its region is SW. 'Area' belongs to the definition, not the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Originally the strip of grass cut by one sweep of a scythe, the word now means any wide stretch of land.

entries.clue: Woman with religious education for example? That’s probably true (1,4,3)

blocks.note: Ida is a woman's name
RE = religious education, the British school subject
say = for example, as in 'a fruit, say an apple'

annotation.surface: A woman who teaches religion, perhaps, and someone concedes it may be so.
annotation.walkthrough: RE is religious education, the subject taught in British schools.
annotation.definitionFit: 'I dare say' is a phrase meaning 'that is probably so'.

entries.clue: Italian duo I ignored possibly getting excessive praise (9)

indicatorNotes.ignored: one I is ignored, so it is dropped from the fodder
indicatorNotes.possibly: possibly signals the letters could form something else

blocks.note: ITALIAN DUO with one I removed
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A pair of Italians, overlooked by the narrator, may be getting fulsome flattery.
annotation.walkthrough: Only one of the three I's in ITALIAN DUO goes; the remaining nine letters are rearranged.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word comes from Latin adulari, to fawn, so the praise is by nature over the top.

entries.clue: Liam regularly studies poorly, showing apathy (9)

indicatorNotes.regularly: take letters at regular intervals: the first and third
indicatorNotes.poorly: studies done poorly are done badly, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: L(i)A(m): first and third letters
STUDIES rearranged

annotation.surface: A student called Liam keeps working badly because he cannot be bothered.
annotation.walkthrough: Liam is just a source of letters; the alternate letters L and A start the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Lassitude is weariness and lack of interest or energy, close to apathy.

entries.clue: Added condition for one on a bicycle (5)

blocks.note: legal sense: an extra clause tacked onto a contract or bill
a cyclist, the person sitting on the bike

annotation.surface: A bike hire firm adds a clause to the contract for cyclists.
annotation.walkthrough: A rider in legal language is an extra condition tacked onto a document.
annotation.definitionFit: A rider is an added clause and also someone who rides.

entries.clue: Totally even patch of warm colour (5)

blocks.note: the carpenter's sense: two surfaces exactly level with each other
a reddening, as of the cheeks

annotation.surface: A painter checking a smooth, level patch of warm colour on a wall.
annotation.walkthrough: The first sense is the carpenter's: a shelf flush with the wall is exactly level with it.
annotation.definitionFit: Flush means exactly level, and a flush is a rosy glow on the skin.

entries.clue: Very slim coat for Luke given a comfortable place (7)

indicatorNotes.coat for: a coat is the outside layer, so take Luke's outer letters

blocks.note: L(uk)E: the outside letters
a nest is a snug, comfortable place, and a is taken as printed

annotation.surface: A thin coat is handed to a man called Luke, who is found somewhere cosy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Very slim' asks for the superlative, so LEANEST rather than lean. 'Given' just tacks A NEST onto the end.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the superlative: 'very slim' stands in for 'most lean'.

entries.clue: Grades too devised for entrance to theatre (5,4)

indicatorNotes.devised: devised means made up or worked out afresh, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: Grading criteria are also drawn up for admission to drama school.
annotation.walkthrough: The stage door is the back entrance actors use, where fans wait for autographs.
annotation.definitionFit: A literal description: the door at the back that leads straight to the stage and dressing rooms, used by cast and crew.

entries.clue: Adult starts to wander nervously among lot (5-2)

indicatorNotes.starts to: the starts of the next two words are taken
indicatorNotes.among: the letters go among, inside, the word for lot

blocks.note: a lot = a group, as in 'that lot'; it is split GRO…UP
first letters of Wander and Nervously, placed inside

annotation.surface: A grown man wanders anxiously through a crowd.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lot' is not a large amount here but a set of people, as in 'that lot over there'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the informal, often childish word for an adult, someone who has finished growing.

entries.clue: One got upset about hospital being very busy (2,3,2)

indicatorNotes.upset: upset letters are knocked over and rearranged
indicatorNotes.about: the rearranged letters go about the hospital's H

blocks.note: anagram fodder, arranged as ONT…EGO
H = hospital, as on road signs; it sits inside

annotation.surface: Someone got upset at the hospital for being rushed off their feet.
annotation.walkthrough: The anagram of ONE GOT goes around H, giving ONT(H)EGO.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone on the go is constantly active and busy.

entries.clue: Brass instrument player has time for grand household retainer (6)

indicatorNotes.has time for grand: the word has T (time) in place of G (grand)

blocks.note: a bugler plays the bugle
T = time, as in physics formulas
G = grand, slang for a thousand pounds; it is the letter swapped out

annotation.surface: A bugler has swapped music for serving a stately home.
annotation.walkthrough: BUGLER with its G replaced by T gives BUTLER. A grand is slang for a thousand, written G.
annotation.definitionFit: A retainer is an old word for a servant kept on in a household; the butler is the chief of them.

entries.clue: Chap, one with hint about right treatment for hands (8)

indicatorNotes.about: the hint goes about, around, the letter for right

blocks.note: a chap is a man
I = one, the Roman numeral
a cue is a hint or prompt; it is split CU…E
R = right; it sits inside CUE

annotation.surface: A man with a hint about the right way to look after your hands.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Right' reads as correct in the surface; it is only the letter R, and 'about' puts the hint around it.
annotation.definitionFit: From Latin manus, hand, and cura, care: the word literally means care of the hands.

entries.clue: Make a speech about last of men that’s decorated (6)

indicatorNotes.about: the speech goes about, around, the letter
indicatorNotes.last of: take the last letter of men

blocks.note: to orate is to make a speech; it is split OR…ATE
the final letter of meN, placed inside

annotation.surface: A speaker addresses the last of the men who have been awarded medals.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Decorated' reads as honoured with medals; it is the adjective for elaborately adorned.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: from Latin ornare, to adorn, describing something heavily adorned.

entries.clue: Unstable reign in African country (5)

indicatorNotes.Unstable: unstable letters will not stay put, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 5 letters

annotation.surface: A shaky regime holds power in an African nation.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a plausible news line, which hides that 'unstable' is working on the letters of REIGN.
annotation.definitionFit: Niger is a landlocked country in West Africa.

entries.clue: Trump, say, near ground interrupted by people (10)

indicatorNotes.ground: ground up, the letters are broken and rearranged
indicatorNotes.interrupted by: the other word breaks into the middle of them

blocks.note: NEAR rearranged, split RE…AN
the public = the people; it sits inside

annotation.surface: Donald Trump stands close to a site overrun by the crowd.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Trump' looks like a card-game verb; with 'say' marking an example it is Donald Trump, a Republican. RE(PUBLIC)AN.
annotation.definitionFit: Donald Trump is a Republican, a member of the US Republican Party.

entries.clue: Merriment in single entertainer? Not entirely! (4)

indicatorNotes.in: the answer is inside the words that follow
indicatorNotes.Not entirely: only part of the phrase is used

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of the first word into the start of the second

annotation.walkthrough: sin(GLE E)ntertainer: the answer spans the gap between the two words.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean high-spirited delight.

entries.clue: Man captivated by a pastry dish, fundamentally (2,5)

indicatorNotes.captivated by: held captive, the man sits inside the other word

blocks.note: a + TART, a pastry dish; split AT…ART
he = a man, the male pronoun; it sits inside

annotation.walkthrough: 'Captivated' suggests being charmed, but here it only means held inside. 'Fundamentally' sits at the end, where it reads like an afterthought, yet it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: At heart means fundamentally, in one's true nature.

entries.clue: Special pointed item for garden bird (7)

blocks.note: SP = special, a standard abbreviation
an arrow has a pointed tip

annotation.surface: A special spiked ornament for the garden.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Garden' sits in the surface as the place an ornament goes; it belongs to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: The house sparrow is one of the commonest garden birds.
